relevance_note: Case report of a man with GAMT deficiency and his sibling: 'confirmed the diagnosis of guanidinoacetate methyltransferase (GAMT) deficiency, with a homozygous c.327G>A mutation' and 'His older sibling was subsequently found to have the same homozygous mutation.'
method_note: Built by hand-written Python in scratch; table-row spans for Table 1 were sliced from the paper lines and checked against the table. Two in-scope people: the unnamed case-report patient ('patient') and his older sibling of unstated sex ('sibling of patient'). The paper prints the variant as 'c.327G>A' (HTML entity from conversion); value recorded as c.327G>A, span kept verbatim. The gene tested is printed as 'the CCDS gene'; gene_symbol recorded as GAMT from the diagnosis sentence. The sibling's variant is 'the same homozygous mutation' (spans: the patient's variant string plus the sibling sentence). Publication year is not printed in the document (year null); n_patients_reported null because the authors give no count. Brain MRI was 'normal' (childhood); under D-27 a normal investigation as a whole excludes nothing more specific, so the three MRI checklist items are not reported and no MRI feature row was emitted. 'Movement disorder ... not present in our case' recorded as an excluded feature but not used to exclude dystonia, ataxia, chorea or tremor; 'flexed posturing of the hands' recorded as stated, not as dystonia; 'relatively normal gait' not used. 'Frequent hand clasping' mapped to the stereotypies checklist item (judgement). 'Learning difficulties' (UK usage) mapped to developmental delay or intellectual disability for both people. Table 1 values below/above the printed normal range were recorded as abnormal; plasma creatine 12 (range 10-100) not recorded. Post-treatment Table 2 values not recorded as features. Karyotype, Angelman testing and array-CGH were negative investigations, not recorded as features. No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: various antiepileptic drugs without control (sodium valproate; phenytoin, lamotrigine, levetiracetam and carbamazepine failed); palliative corpus callosectomy at age 14 (seizure free for two weeks, then seizures returned); oral creatine increased gradually to 24g daily in divided doses, without significant dietary alteration; seizure free for four months at nine months of treatment
span: At the age of 14 he underwent corpus callosectomy as a palliative treatment for his seizures. He was seizure free for two weeks post-operatively before seizures returned to baseline frequency and severity.
He was taking sodium valproate, and it was noted that the following drugs had also failed to control his epilepsy: phenytoin, lamotrigine, levetiracetam and carbamazepine.
The patient was started on oral creatine, which was increased gradually to a dose of 24g daily, in divided doses.
significant alterations in diet were not felt to be appropriate
Nine months after starting treatment, he has been seizure free for four months.
